### Project Name

nono

### Project Description

nono is a complete agent runtime security tool. Secure your agents, their tools, their credentials, and the skills and instructions they follow, with low latency, a minimal footprint, and zero setup. Kernel-enforced sandboxing is the foundation for a complete workflow of protection, verification, audit, and recovery. It secures coding and general-purpose agents, custom agent frameworks, and MCP servers through composable policies that remain outside the agent’s control. Supported agents include Goose, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Pi, and others. Developers can also use nono with custom agents built on frameworks such as ADK, Pydantic AI, and LangChain.

**Origin and history:** created in February 2026 by Luke Hinds. The project now has 1,800+ commits, 80 releases, and contributions from 100+ developers. Design changes go through a public proposal process (NEPs). Development happens in the open on GitHub. Luke previously created Sigstore and transferred it to the Linux Foundation, bringing experience in building open-source security infrastructure and guiding its transition to neutral governance.


### Preferred Lifecycle Stage (if known)

Sandbox

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

AAIF brings together shared, neutral infrastructure for agentic AI. nono contributes runtime security across agents and frameworks: controlling tool execution, protecting credentials, verifying skills and instructions, and recording auditable evidence. Its composable policies give developers and enterprises a consistent way to secure agent workflows. Under AAIF, agent developers, tool builders, and adopters can jointly shape these controls through open governance, independent of any single vendor.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

- **goose:** nono provides runtime security for goose sessions, including sandboxing on Linux.
- **MCP:** nono can confine an MCP server to the files, network endpoints and credentials it needs, which complements MCP's authorization model at the OS layer.
- **AGENTS.md:** nono uses Sigstore signatures to verify the provenance (source code origin) and integrity of policy-covered agent instruction files and reject unsigned or tampered content at the system access level. 
- **agentgateway / Agent Router:** these govern agent traffic on the network. nono governs what the agent process can do on the host. Together they cover both sides of an agent's reach. While nono also introduces network filtering at the host level, nono can and often is run without these features and instead relays traffic through upstream to an existing gateway or router for network control.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Use cases: running agents with least privilege; per-command policies for agents in enterprise toolchains; confining MCP servers and tool executions; running agents in CI and production with an auditable policy record.

Community testimonials:
- **Datadog:** "nono is the only sandbox that gives us both fine-grained, per-command policies and sophisticated credential management that fits existing, complex real-world toolchains." - James Carnegie, Staff Security Engineer.
- **Okta:** "Security is embedded in everything we build at Okta. nono gives us the confidence to innovate with AI agents by isolating their execution in a highly secure, policy-controlled sandbox. It ensures our credentials remain locked down and protected, without sacrificing developer velocity." - Leonardo Zanivan, Principal Engineer.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

GitHub Actions: `ci.yml` runs build, lint, clippy and tests across Linux and macOS on every PR. Additional workflows cover Nix builds, container images, PR linting and labelling, and SPIRE integration tests. Releases are tag-driven (`release.yml`): the build matrix produces Linux and macOS binaries, `attest-release.yml` attaches Sigstore build-provenance attestations, and packaging is published to Homebrew, AUR, RPM and Nix. The changelog is generated with git-cliff. Dependabot handles dependency updates.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

All PRs must first have a related issue. For large changes we require a NEP (nono enhancement proposal): https://github.com/nolabs-ai/nono/tree/main/neps

NEPs (nono Enhancement Proposals) in `neps/`, defined by `NEP-0000`,  are required for changes too large or security-consequential for a PR description, and must include an explicit security review. 

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

https://github.com/nolabs-ai/nono/issues

### External Project Dependencies

A Rust workspace with 553 third-party crates (cargo metadata, 16 Oct 2026). Every licence is permissive except three crates under MPL-2.0 (weak, file-level copyleft):
- MIT and/or Apache-2.0 (including dual licences): ~500
- Unicode-3.0: 18
- Unlicense OR MIT: 12
- ISC, BSD-2/3-Clause, Zlib, 0BSD, MIT-0, CC0, BSL-1.0 (as alternatives): remainder
- MPL-2.0: `cbindgen` (build-time only, for C bindings), `colored`, `option-ext`
- CDLA-Permissive-2.0: `webpki-roots`, `webpki-root-certs` (Mozilla CA bundle data)

We will seek to take other Approaches if an exception is not possible.

Key dependencies: tokio, serde, landlock, nix, sigstore-sign/verify, rustls.

### Lifecycle Stage Evidence

## The problem
AI agents now run with the full authority of the developer or service that launches them: every file, every credential, every network endpoint. The isolation tools that exist, containers and VMs, are too heavy for the interactive agent loop. So in practice most agents run unconfined, and each agent vendor builds its own partial, incompatible sandbox. There is no shared model for what an agent should be allowed to do, and no neutral implementation of one.

## What nono is
A kernel-enforced, capability-based sandbox that wraps any agent process: It needs no daemon, container or VM, and starts in milliseconds. Policies cover filesystem, network, commands and credentials. A credential proxy keeps secrets out of the agent's reach, an audit log records actions, and Sigstore can verify signed instruction files. 

## Who uses it
- **Developers** running Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, goosem Pi and other agent CLIs or frameworks both hosted, locally or in CI
- **Platform and security teams** who need per-command policy and credential isolation to let agents into real toolchains. Datadog and Okta engineers use nono today
- **Agent and harness builders** who want a sandbox they can embed rather than build, including through the C bindings.


### Security

- OpenSSF Best Practices badge: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/13332. 
- SECURITY.md defines private disclosure through GitHub Security Advisories and a documented threat model. 
- Releases carry Sigstore attestations. 
- Third-party audit by OSTIF: **will be made public late October**.
- Security-critical changes require unanimous maintainer approval
- All PRs recieve a security specific CI scan https://github.com/nolabs-ai/nogent (we are willing to host elsewhere if needed)
